text:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: P1 GPU OOM on runtime-prod-3 (us-west1). Service: inference-serving. Symptoms: repeated container restarts, cpp runtime crashed with CUDA OOM during prefill.

maria (oncall): I'm paged, taking ownership. Confirming impact and whether customers are affected.

devon (sre): I'm oncall rotation - on it. I see node runtime-prod-3 is flapping, kubelet reports container restarts ~every 3m. Metrics: gpu memory at 100% before crash, OOM logs show prefill allocation failure.

kai (runtime-eng): Logs from the runtime: `CUDA error: out of memory` during KV-cache allocate in prefill path for model `redwood-70b-v1` when seq_len gets large. One recent request had a huge user-supplied prompt (estimated ~65k tokens) which pushed the KV cache allocation beyond available VRAM. Container restarted after the failed malloc.

lex (support): We already have a customer ticket from AcmeCorp reporting 502s and 'container restarted' on their inference calls starting ~00:12. They hit a single request that was extremely long (attachments + context).

maria (oncall): OK, immediate mitigations: 1) remove traffic from runtime-prod-3, 2) set a temporary reject rule for requests above a token threshold, 3) triage any queued restarts. Devon, can you cordon/drain the node? Kai, can you provide a quick runtime config we can flip?

devon (sre): Cordon done: `kubectl cordon runtime-prod-3` and started draining non-critical pods. Moving active model pods to other nodes. Scaling cluster by +2 GPU nodes to absorb traffic while we investigate.

kai (runtime-eng): Quick mitigation we can toggle via console: enable `prefill_stream_trim=true` and set `max_input_tokens=65536`. This will cause the runtime to truncate extremely long prefill prefixes and explicitly reject >65k tokens with 413. Patch snippet we can push immediately:

```yaml
runtime_settings:
  prefill_stream_trim: true
  max_input_tokens: 65536
  reject_large_prefill: true
```

kai (runtime-eng): I'll push a canary to 10% of traffic in us-west1 first. That should stop the immediate OOMs while we root-cause the large requests.

maria (oncall): Do it. Devon, can you confirm node is stable after draining?

devon (sre): Node drained successfully. No further restarts after pods relocated. New GPU nodes are provisioning; autoscaler triggered +2.

lex (support): I'll send a short customer update to AcmeCorp: "We've identified large single-request contexts causing runtime OOMs and restarts. We've moved your traffic off the affected host and enabled protective limits to prevent recurrence. If you can share the exact request, we can help advise on trimming strategies. No data loss, but some requests may have failed—we're monitoring." OK to send?

kai (runtime-eng): Yes. Also recommend telling them we can enable server-side prefix trimming or a prompt preprocessing step.

maria (oncall): Canary toggle complete: `prefill_stream_trim` on for 10% -> monitoring. No OOMs in canary pods so far. Rolling to 100% in 5m if stable.

(5m later)

maria (oncall): Rolling to 100% now.

devon (sre): Rolling complete. No new OOMs in the last 12m for the cluster. The flapping on runtime-prod-3 stopped after drain. We'll keep it cordoned until followup.

lex (support): Sent customer update to AcmeCorp at 00:42. They acknowledged and provided the failing request payload; it's ~78k tokens including attachments. They've agreed to a short-term limit while we implement a better server-side preprocessing.

kai (runtime-eng): Root cause analysis notes in-flight: runtime didn't enforce an upper bound on prefill length; extremely long single requests can blow the KV cache allocation on GPU. Short-term patch: enforced max_input_tokens + prefill trimming. Mid-term: quota + better telemetry to surface per-request token counts and a graceful prefill stream that can fallback to CPU or smaller model if request is huge. We'll prepare a code change and aim for a stable rollout tomorrow.

maria (oncall): Impact summary for incident log: Severity P1, customer-facing errors for at least AcmeCorp (single major request resulting in 502s), cluster-level container restarts on one node, mitigated by draining node and enabling runtime limits. No persisted data loss.

lex (support): Draft customer-facing postmortem blurb: "At ~00:12 UTC we observed a GPU OOM caused by a very large prefill request which led to container restarts on one host. We drained the host, applied protective limits, and restored normal service by ~00:45 UTC. We're implementing safeguards to reject or gracefully handle extremely large contexts going forward." Anyone want to edit?

kai (runtime-eng): Add: "We will add per-request token logging to metrics and an automatic fallback path to route oversized requests to a CPU fallback or smaller model."

maria (oncall): Next steps: - Kai: prepare runtime PR for token logging + fallback (owner) - Devon: uncordon after postmortem and safe window (owner) - Lex: keep AcmeCorp updated and close the ticket when we release the PR.

sam (oncall-next): I'm taking next shift. Thanks for the handoff, Maria. I'll monitor the alert channel and the canary dashboard for the next 4h.

maria (oncall): Handing off to @sam. Incident moved to monitoring. Postmortem required, add to the incidents backlog. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident P1 acknowledged by maria (oncall). Escalation closed.

(End of thread)
